context:
Build as a table renderer with inline mini-bars rather than a traditional chart:

1. Create SparklineColumn (name, values dict[platform, float], higher_is_better) and
   SparklineTableData (platforms, columns) dataclasses.
2. Create ASCIISparklineTable(ASCIIChartBase) with render().
3. For each column, normalize values to 0.0-1.0 range and render as a 1-4 character
   vertical block using LOWER_BLOCK_CHARS (▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█).
4. Respect higher_is_better flag: for latency metrics (lower is better), invert the
   normalization so the best platform gets the tallest bar.
5. Color the best value green (#1b9e77) and worst red (#d95f02) per column.
6. Add from_normalized_results() factory that populates columns from standard metrics.

Column width calculation should be dynamic: metric name width + sparkline bar width +
value width, constrained to fit within terminal width. If too many columns, truncate
lower-priority columns with "..." indicator.
description:
Add a new ASCII chart type that displays a compact leaderboard table where each row
is a platform and each column is a metric, with inline sparkline-style mini-bars
showing relative values. This combines the information density of a table with
visual comparison cues.

This is the format used by ClickBench's dashboard and most database comparison sites.
When comparing many platforms across many dimensions (total time, geometric mean, P99,
cost, success rate, data load time), a pure table is hard to scan visually, while
individual charts for each metric create information overload.

Example output:
```
Platform Comparison Overview
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Platform   Total(ms)   GeoMean    P99(ms)   Load(s)   Success
DuckDB     ▇  1,240    ▇  56      ▅ 120     ▂  2.1    ████ 100%
Polars     ▆  1,580    ▆  72      ▇ 310     ▁  1.2    ████ 100%
SQLite     ▃  4,820    ▃ 219      ▃ 450     ▅  8.4    ███░  95%
Pandas     ▁ 12,300    ▁ 559      ▁ 980     ▃  5.2    ██░░  82%
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
▇=best  ▁=worst  (bars scaled per column)
```

This is distinct from the Summary Box (single run stats), the Heatmap (query-level
detail), and the Bar Chart (one metric at a time). The sparkline table uniquely
combines multiple aggregate metrics in a single compact view with embedded
visual encoding.

anti_patterns.instead: accept a flexible list of SparklineColumn instances

anti_patterns.dont: use full-width bar charts per cell
anti_patterns.why: the value of this chart is compactness

preserves.behavior: ASCIISummaryBox behavior unchanged (sparkline table is multi-platform overview, summary box is single-run aggregate stats)
All 9 existing chart types continue to render identically
render_ascii_chart() in exporters.py handles all existing chart_type strings

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c "from benchbox.core.visualization.ascii.sparkline_table import ASCIISparklineTable, SparklineColumn, SparklineTableData; cols = [SparklineColumn('Total(ms)', {'DuckDB': 1240, 'Polars': 1580}, False), SparklineColumn('Success', {'DuckDB': 100, 'Polars': 100}, True)]; data = SparklineTableData(['DuckDB', 'Polars'], cols); chart = ASCIISparklineTable(data=data); print(chart.render())"
verifications.description: New chart class renders without error
verifications.expected: Rendered table with sparkline bars and values
